entries.summary: Wormwood (Apsinthion) is a herb in Book III of De Materia Medica. Modern identification: Artemisia absinthium. Dioscorides discusses the root, juice/sap, whole herb. Preparations he mentions include decoction, infusion, in wine, with honey, with vinegar. He describes it as warming, astringent. He lists uses relating to the stomach and digestion, aches and swellings, bites and poisons, the liver and spleen, the eyes. Toxic or dangerous: recorded for history only and never used for cooking.
